name: Unleashed! A Cappella
description: UW Seattle's only non-audition a cappella choir, singing contemporary and classical pieces and styles in between. It calls itself a family of performers who love to sing and laugh together.
meeting_schedule: Rehearsals Wednesdays 7:30-9:30pm in the music building
fit_reason: Singers of any experience level who want a friendly, no-audition choir.

steps: Show up to a Wednesday rehearsal
Or email unleashd@u.washington.edu / join the mailing list

name: Furmata A Cappella
description: UW's competitive co-ed a cappella group; it placed second at the 2025 International Championship of Collegiate A Cappella (ICCA) finals in New York. Members arrange and choreograph their own sets.
meeting_schedule: Multi-hour practices three to five days a week (per UW 2025 profile); exact times couldn't confirm
fit_reason: Serious singers wanting a highly selective, nationally competitive a cappella team.

steps: Audition (fewer than 10% accepted, per UW profile)
Ask about audition dates at open rehearsals or via HuskyLink

interest_areas: Research/competitive teams (robotics, case competitions, Model UN)

name: Stage Notes
description: UW's first and only student-run musical theatre organization, producing musicals and hosting events since 2011. Its 2026-27 production is Into the Woods.

commitment.hours_per_week: ~12-13 hrs/wk when cast in a show

meeting_schedule: Into the Woods rehearsals Mon-Thu 6-8pm (Thu possibly to 9pm) and Sun 12-4pm; performances Feb 3-7, 2027
fit_reason: Students who love musicals and want to act, sing, dance or crew a full production.

application.deadline: Into the Woods auditions Oct 12-14 with callbacks Oct 15-16 (passed); next audition dates unknown
steps: Read the audition packet on the Linktree
Fill out the audition form and attend one vocal day plus a dance slot
Callbacks by email invitation

name: Salsa Club at UW
description: Beginner-friendly Latin dance RSO focused on Salsa and Bachata; meetings combine lessons with social dancing, open to any UW student regardless of experience.
dues: $4 drop-in; $18/quarter for Salsa or Bachata; $25/quarter for both (includes quarterly social). Pricing shown with a Spring 2025 form, confirm current rates; contact club if cost is an issue
meeting_schedule: Weekly lessons: Tuesday Salsa, Thursday Bachata (times couldn't confirm)
fit_reason: Beginners and social dancers who want affordable weekly salsa and bachata lessons.

steps: Drop in to a lesson ($4) or buy a quarterly membership
Fill out the membership form on the Memberships page

name: Tap Club at UW
description: Aims to make tap dance more accessible at UW through performances, events and workshops, with an emphasis on inclusivity and tap's history. Holds a club performance each year at the end of winter quarter.
meeting_schedule: Four classes per month (days/times couldn't confirm); annual show at end of winter quarter
fit_reason: Curious beginners or experienced tappers; no experience or tap shoes needed to start.

steps: Attend a class (all levels welcome)
Follow @tapclubuw for class times

name: LUX: Film Production Club
description: Student filmmaking club founded in 2016 whose mission is to cultivate a space where UW students can meet people and make films; produces quarterly films chosen by member vote plus independent shorts.
dues: No dues listed (confirm with officers); screening tickets $5 minimum, free if you worked on a screened film
meeting_schedule: Regular club meetings (times couldn't confirm; posted in Slack/Google Calendar); end-of-quarter screenings
fit_reason: Aspiring directors, actors and crew of any experience who want to make short films.

steps: Join the LUX Slack from the website
Come to a meeting and pitch or join a production

name: Swing Kids at UW
description: Student group teaching Lindy Hop swing dancing through affordable weekly lessons, quarterly dances and social outings such as nights at Reverie Ballroom.
meeting_schedule: Weekly lessons (day/time couldn't confirm) plus quarterly dances and outings
fit_reason: Anyone wanting a fun, social partner dance with no experience required.

steps: Join the Discord or follow @SwingKidsatUW
Drop in to a weekly lesson

name: Chinese Student Association at the University of Washington (CSA UW)
description: CSA UW aims to build awareness of Chinese culture, strengthen Chinese and Chinese American identity, and foster connections within the university and wider community, celebrating culture through food, music and stories. It runs events such as Lantern Festival, Dumpling Night, a Lunar New Year Gala and Bonfire, plus smaller CSA family groups.
dues: No membership fee described; optional $5 CSA Perk Card (sponsor discounts) sold at the Red Square table
meeting_schedule: No regular meeting schedule listed; quarterly events plus optional CSA families; Red Square tabling Mon-Fri 11am-2pm
fit_reason: Students wanting Chinese cultural events, festivals and a friendly social community.

steps: Attend a CSA event
Optionally buy a Perk Card at the Red Square table
Optionally join a CSA family group

name: Vietnamese Student Association at the University of Washington (VSAUW)
description: VSAUW describes itself as a cultural, social and civically engaged organization that has fostered community among students and the greater Seattle community since the 1980s. Its largest annual event is a cultural pageant (Phở King / Hoa Khôi), and it runs ACCE family groups.
dues: Optional paid membership (shirt + card, sponsor/event discounts); price not listed; membership not required to attend events
meeting_schedule: General meetings every two weeks (check Instagram for dates)
fit_reason: Students interested in Vietnamese culture, family groups and big cultural showcase events.

steps: Attend a general meeting or event
Optionally purchase a membership
Optionally join an ACCE family

name: First Nations @ UW
description: An undergraduate intertribal registered student organization that hosts on- and off-campus events to educate the community about Native cultures, raise awareness of issues affecting Native communities, and uphold members' customs and traditions. It is best known for its annual Spring Powwow, which draws Native people from across the U.S. and Canada.
meeting_schedule: General meetings every Wednesday at 6:00 pm, alternating between the Native Room (Samuel E. Kelly Ethnic Cultural Center) and Intellectual House
fit_reason: Native students and supporters wanting intertribal community and to help run the Spring Powwow.

steps: Come to a Wednesday general meeting
Join the Discord or follow Instagram for updates

name: iQueeries
description: A registered student organization at the UW Information School that aims to provide a safe, positive and nurturing space for LGBTQIA and supportive ally students; it states that all identities and experiences are welcome. It hosts on-campus and online events each quarter, such as queer trivia and board game nights.
meeting_schedule: No regular meeting time listed; events held throughout the academic year (see the group's calendar)
fit_reason: LGBTQIA+ students and allies, especially in the iSchool, wanting low-key social events.

steps: Join the mailing list or follow on Instagram
Drop in to an event

name: Huskies for Opportunities in Prison Education (HOPE)
description: UW students and community members providing education on the prison-industrial complex and civic engagement, working in solidarity with incarcerated organizers. Projects include Books Beyond Bars, prison visits, a prison labor campaign and legislative work.
meeting_schedule: Mondays 4:30-5:30 pm in Savery Hall (2026-27)
fit_reason: Students who care about criminal justice reform, prison education and grassroots advocacy.

steps: Attend a Monday meeting in Savery Hall
Or email hopeuwseattle@gmail.com

name: Institutional Climate Action UW Chapter
description: Student-led climate justice group campaigning for a fossil-free university, including fossil fuel divestment and a faster UW decarbonization timeline. Runs teach-ins, petitions, film screenings and direct actions.
meeting_schedule: Thursdays 6:00 pm in Savery Hall 156; open to anyone
fit_reason: Students ready to organize campaigns and take action on climate justice at UW.

steps: Show up to a Thursday 6 pm meeting in SAV 156
Sign up for the newsletter via the Linktree

name: Engineers Without Borders USA – University of Washington Chapter
description: Student chapter driving community development abroad through engineering and cultural exchange, with international projects in Bolivia, Haiti and Malawi and local UW projects like solar charging stations and a UW Farm high tunnel. Open to all majors.
meeting_schedule: Wednesdays 5:30-6:30 pm in MEB 248
fit_reason: Hands-on builders of any major who want engineering projects that serve real communities.

steps: Attend a Wednesday meeting to get the New Member Application doc
Join communication channels, describe interests and submit the application
Project leads review in about one week

name: WashPIRG at UW
description: UW's student public interest group since 1976, running non-partisan grassroots campaigns with professional staff, such as the New Voters Project, Make Textbooks Affordable, Hunger and Homelessness, and Save the Orcas.
meeting_schedule: Autumn 2026: Mondays 6:30 pm in MEB 238
fit_reason: Students wanting to lobby, register voters and run issue campaigns without party politics.

steps: Sign up at washpirgstudents.org/volunteer or join via HuskyLink/Discord
Come to a Monday meeting
Optional: apply for a campus internship

name: Partners In Health Engage of UW
description: Global health RSO supporting Partners In Health's mission to make health care a human right through advocacy, fundraising, community building and global health education.
meeting_schedule: Biweekly meetings (day/time couldn't confirm)
fit_reason: Pre-health and policy students who want to advocate and fundraise for global health equity.

steps: Follow @pihengageuw for meeting info
Attend a biweekly meeting

name: Perfect Pair @ UW
description: UW chapter of a national nonprofit that matches university students one-on-one with older adults to build intergenerational connections and reduce isolation; members also make cards for local retirement homes.
meeting_schedule: Pairs meet regularly, often weekly or every two weeks
fit_reason: Students wanting a steady one-on-one friendship volunteering with a senior.

steps: Join via HuskyLink
Go through the chapter's matching process with an older adult

name: BeautifyUdub (Beautify UW)
description: Student group that grew from a small first-year litter cleanup into about 135 cleanups on campus and in Seattle parks, neighborhoods and beaches, plus clothing swaps, UW Farm events and producer-responsibility advocacy. 2026 Husky Sustainability Award recipient.
meeting_schedule: couldn't confirm (asks members for 30 minutes of cleanup every week)
fit_reason: Anyone wanting quick, low-commitment, hands-on ways to clean up campus and Seattle.

steps: Follow @beautifyudub for cleanup times
Show up to a cleanup

name: Education Transforming Community Health (ETCH)
description: Student group working with local shelters and community organizations to make health information easier to understand, running health education sessions for adults experiencing homelessness in Seattle. All majors welcome; no healthcare experience required.
meeting_schedule: Weekly health education sessions; volunteers asked to attend at least one per month for 6 months (per 2016 post; confirm)
fit_reason: Pre-health and public health students who want direct community health outreach experience.

steps: Meet officers at tabling or email etchseattle@gmail.com
Join an upcoming session

name: Huskies for Housing
description: RSO advocating on housing justice and homelessness and supporting Seattle's unhoused community through food, hygiene and clothing drives, partnering with the UW Food Pantry, Tent City 3 and local groups.
meeting_schedule: No general meeting time listed; food-donation tabling Mon & Wed 1-4 pm outside Alder District Market
fit_reason: Students who want to act on homelessness through donation drives, mutual aid and advocacy.

steps: Fill out the New Member Sign Up Form on the website
Join the club Discord

name: Students Expressing Environmental Dedication (SEED)
description: Residence-hall sustainability group working with residents and Housing & Food Services on projects like OZZI reusable container machines and in-room compost bin checkouts. Each residential community has a representative on the SEED committee.
meeting_schedule: Thursdays 5:00-6:00 pm, Spratlen Hall 313
fit_reason: Dorm residents who want to make campus housing greener.

application.deadline: Start of Autumn quarter (community reps selected)
steps: Use the Join Us page on the RCSA site or email rcsasus@uw.edu
Community reps are selected at the start of Autumn quarter
